target.title: fix(browser): honor abort signal during CDP handshake retry backoff
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`withCdpSocket` in `extensions/browser/src/browser/cdp.helpers.ts` retries failed WebSocket handshakes on a 200ms→3s exponential backoff (with jitter, up to 2 extra attempts) using an unabortable `sleep`. The browser permissions route (`routes/permissions.ts`) already receives the per-request `AbortSignal` and calls `params.signal.throwIfAborted()` around every other stage of `grantPermissions` — but the `withCdpSocket` call passed only `commandTimeoutMs`, so an aborted permission grant still waited out the remaining handshake backoff before the abort was noticed.

## Why This Change Was Made

`CdpSocketOptions` gains an optional `signal`, the backoff sleep uses `sleepWithAbort(ms, opts?.signal)` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/runtime-env` (the same helper and import path as the merged #109710 Playwright-click and #109617 tab-discovery browser fixes), and the permissions route passes its `params.signal` through. An abort landing mid-backoff now rejects the sleep with the stable `Error("aborted")` from `sleepWithAbort`, which propagates out of `withCdpSocket` before any further socket is opened. Callers that pass no signal see zero behavior change — `sleepWithAbort(ms, undefined)` degenerates to the plain timer, and already-aborted signals are handled by the helper itself.

## Changes

- Thread an optional `signal` through `CdpSocketOptions`; handshake retry backoff sleeps via `sleepWithAbort`.
- Pass the request `signal` at the `grantPermissions` CDP call site.
- Regression test in `cdp.helpers.internal.test.ts`: a real `ws` `WebSocketServer` on 127.0.0.1 always rejects handshakes with 503; `withCdpSocket` runs with `handshakeRetries: 5` and a 30s retry delay; abort fires once the first rejection lands inside the backoff. Asserts rejection with `/aborted/`, wall clock under 10s, and exactly one handshake attempt (no second socket).

## User Impact

Cancelling a browser permission request (or its page/route operation timing out) while Chrome is unreachable no longer lingers through the remaining handshake retry backoff; the route tears down promptly instead of opening doomed sockets.

## Evidence

Exact head: `35432ce27de1131cccb352e8a82e099b191064dc`.

**Outside-runner behavior proof** — the production `withCdpSocket` is driven directly (no test runner, no mocks) via `node --import tsx` against a real loopback `ws` WebSocket server whose `verifyClient` rejects every handshake with 503 and counts attempts. The abort fires the moment the first rejected handshake lands inside the 3000ms backoff.

After fix — abort mid-backoff rejects in 1ms with the abort reason, exactly one handshake attempt, no second socket:

```text
$ TSX_TSCONFIG_PATH=tsconfig.json node --import tsx /tmp/cdp-abort-proof.mts; echo "EXIT=$?"
[proof] loopback CDP WebSocket server: ws://127.0.0.1:40533/devtools/browser/TEST
[proof-server] handshake attempt #1 rejected with 503
[proof] AbortController.abort() fired at +29ms (inside 3000ms backoff)
[proof] outcome expect=after settled=rejected elapsedMs=30 abortAtMs=29 abortToRejectMs=1 handshakeAttempts=1 error="aborted"
[proof] check ok: withCdpSocket rejects (handshake never succeeds)
[proof] check ok: after-fix: rejection is the abort reason ("aborted")
[proof] check ok: after-fix: abort-to-reject 1ms < 1000ms (backoff was 3000ms)
[proof] check ok: after-fix: exactly one handshake attempt, no retry after abort (got 1)
[proof] OK
EXIT=0
```

Before fix (same script with `extensions/browser/src/browser/cdp.helpers.ts` from `upstream/main`, restored immediately after): the abort at +12ms is ignored, handshake attempts #2 and #3 still fire on the full 3000ms schedule, and the rejection arrives 6135ms after the abort with the retry-exhaustion error instead of the abort reason.

```text
[proof-server] handshake attempt #1 rejected with 503
[proof] AbortController.abort() fired at +12ms (inside 3000ms backoff)
[proof-server] handshake attempt #2 rejected with 503
[proof-server] handshake attempt #3 rejected with 503
[proof] outcome expect=before settled=rejected elapsedMs=6147 abortAtMs=12 abortToRejectMs=6135 handshakeAttempts=3 error="Unexpected server response: 503"
[proof] check ok: before-fix: rejection is the retry-exhaustion failure, not the abort ("Unexpected server response: 503")
[proof] check ok: before-fix: abort ignored until backoff elapsed (6147ms >= 3000ms)
[proof] check ok: before-fix: retry fired despite the abort (attempts=3)
[proof] OK (expect=before)
```

Regression tests:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/browser/src/browser/cdp.helpers.internal.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  29 passed (29)
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/permissions.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
```

Same new test against the pre-change implementation (file at `upstream/main`): the abort is ignored, the loop rides out the 30s backoff per attempt, and the run stalls until the 120s Vitest watchdog terminates it — the fixed implementation passes the same test in under 1s against a real loopback WebSocket server (no mocked fetch).

`oxlint` clean on all three changed files; `tsgo` extensions project reports no errors in browser files.

## Intentionally out of scope

- The other `withCdpSocket` call sites (`chrome.ts`, `cdp-page-session.ts`, `chrome.graphics.ts`, `pw-session.ts`, `cdp.ts`) keep their current no-signal behavior; this PR threads the signal only where a real per-request signal already exists and is checked around sibling stages.
- No change to retry counts, the 200ms→3s backoff schedule, jitter, or which handshake errors are retryable (rate-limited 429s still never retry).
